messages.content: Birmingham is wrapped. I need to start the Minneapolis board committee trip: May 19-21, Chicago to MSP, no rental car. Wednesday opening dinner is around 6:30, Thursday full board downtown, and Friday breakouts are expected to end around noon. Can you compare flight and hotel pairings? Main question is event hotel convenience versus a cheaper nearby place with breakfast.
Yes. A couple of quick assumptions before I price this: carry-on only? Standard economy? And are ORD and MDW both acceptable if the flights are nonstop?
Carry-on only, standard economy. ORD is easier, but I would look at MDW if it is materially better. Hotel should be refundable, and I need the total to look defensible for reimbursement.

I found three clean pairings, all no rental car. Estimated totals include round-trip airfare, two hotel nights with taxes, and about $80 for airport rideshares; they do not include meals unless noted.

| Pairing | Flights | Hotel | Est. total | Timing | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| A. Event-hotel easy mode | United ORD-MSP 2:10-3:39; return MSP-ORD 3:20-4:55 | The Marquette/event block, about $533 all-in | ~$851 before breakfast | Hotel by ~4:20 Wed; Friday return is fine if noon end holds | Most convenient, but breakfast extra |
| B. Nearby breakfast value | Same United flights | Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown, about $406 all-in, breakfast included | ~$724 | 6-8 minute walk to meeting hotel | Saves about $125+ even before breakfast value; less seamless in bad weather |
| C. More Friday cushion | Delta ORD-MSP 1:35-3:05; return MSP-ORD 4:10-5:45 | Hyatt Place Downtown, about $386 all-in, breakfast included | ~$692 | Earlier arrival, later return | Best total and cushion, but farther walk/short rideshare to board site |
Can you break out the local logistics? I do not want to save $100 and then spend it on short rideshares all week.

Airport transfers are basically the same for all three: rideshare MSP to downtown is usually 20-30 minutes and roughly $35-$45 each way; light rail is cheaper but less convenient with a work bag. For meeting access: event hotel is zero commute; Hampton is a manageable walk and probably no rideshare unless weather is bad; Hyatt is more like 12-15 minutes on foot, so I would budget one or two $8-$12 short rides if it rains or you are carrying materials. The Hampton savings are unlikely to disappear. Hyatt still saves the most, but its location asks for more tolerance.
What about breakfast and the room basics? I would like coffee in the room and a refrigerator if possible.

Room/food check:

| Hotel | Breakfast | In-room basics | Dinner access |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Marquette/event block | Not included; restaurant breakfast or nearby coffee | Coffee maker listed; mini-fridge appears request-based for the block room, so I would confirm before booking | On-site restaurant/bar plus downtown options |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown | Included hot breakfast | Coffee maker and mini-fridge listed for standard rooms | No full-service restaurant, but several casual restaurants within a short walk |
| Hyatt Place Downtown | Included breakfast | Coffee maker and mini-fridge listed | Bar/light meals on site; more restaurants a few blocks away |
I prefer not to leave Chicago first thing, but I do need to be at the dinner without sweating it.

Then I would not use a late-afternoon outbound. The best fit is either United 2:10-3:39 or Delta 1:35-3:05. Both should put you downtown before 4:30 with a rideshare. American has a later nonstop around 3:05-4:32, but that leaves much less room for delays, check-in, and getting to a 6:30 dinner.
For the return, is the 3:20 too tight if the Friday committee ends at noon and there is a quick lunch?

It works if lunch is truly quick. For a 3:20 MSP departure, I would leave downtown around 1:20; that is comfortable after a noon end, but not if the breakout drifts toward 12:45 or lunch is seated. The Delta 4:10 return is the safer after-lunch choice and still gets you to Chicago before 6:00.
Use the later return in the comparison if the fare is close. I do not need United if the timing is better.

With the 4:10 Delta return, the fare is currently about $226 round trip, about $12 less than the United option I priced. Revised best-value pairing is Delta 1:35-3:05 outbound and 4:10-5:45 return with Hampton or Hyatt. If the event hotel wins, I would still use the Delta return unless Friday becomes firmly noon-and-done.
What are the cancellation terms and the block deadline?

Current hotel terms I found: event block at The Marquette is cancellable until May 16 at 6 p.m., with the block cutoff listed as Apr. 28; Hampton refundable rate cancels until May 17 at 11:59 p.m.; Hyatt refundable rate cancels until May 18 at 3 p.m. I would verify the event block cutoff before relying on it, because those sometimes close early when the room block fills.
Please save this without booking. My likely pick is Hampton if the dinner is not actually in the event hotel.

Saved with no bookings made. Current lean: Hampton Downtown plus the Delta 1:35 outbound and 4:10 return, assuming the Wednesday dinner is nearby rather than inside the event hotel. Event hotel remains the convenience backup, especially if the dinner or Friday checkout logistics move into the building. Next decision points: confirm dinner address, confirm Friday end time, and hold a refundable room before the block cutoff.

messages.content: Minneapolis update: board staff confirmed the Wednesday dinner is two blocks from the event hotel, and Friday committee breakouts may run until 1:00. The block deadline is tomorrow morning. Can you narrow lodging to the final choices and tell me if the off-block savings are still worth it?

Yes. I would narrow to the event hotel and Hampton; Hyatt is a little cheaper but less convenient, so it is not as strong now that Friday may run late.

| Hotel | 2-night lodging estimate | Breakfast | Morning/luggage logistics | Room basics | Trade-off |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Event hotel block, The Marquette | ~$533, plus breakfast | Not included | Meeting in building; easiest bag storage Friday | Coffee maker listed; mini-fridge should be requested/confirmed | Highest cost, lowest friction |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown | ~$406, breakfast included | Included | 6-8 minute walk to event hotel; front desk can store bag after checkout | Coffee maker and mini-fridge listed | Saves about $125 before counting breakfast; modest walk/weather risk |
Can you add a bad-weather rideshare estimate? That is the part I am trying not to undercount.

For Hampton, I would budget $8-$12 per short downtown hop. Worst case: Wednesday dinner return, Thursday morning, Friday morning, and Friday bag pickup could be $35-$50 total. Airport rideshares are the same either way. Even with that weather buffer, Hampton is still likely $75-$110 cheaper than the event hotel, and the included breakfast pushes the practical savings higher.
Does Hampton have a restaurant on site, or is it only breakfast?

Only breakfast, not a full-service restaurant. There are nearby dinner options within a short walk, and the official Wednesday dinner being two blocks from the event hotel helps. The event hotel is better if you want an on-site restaurant/bar for an easy backup after sessions.
Please check the room type too. I do not need anything fancy, but I want coffee and a refrigerator, and a single-bed room is fine.

Hampton’s refundable standard rooms list an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge. A one-king room is available at the quoted rate; two-queen is also available for the same estimate. I am not seeing a one-queen refundable room at that price. The event block room lists coffee; the mini-fridge is the item I would put in as a request rather than treat as guaranteed.
Then recommend one hold. I am comfortable walking if the savings are real, but Friday luggage cannot become annoying.

Recommendation: hold Hampton refundable. The savings remain real even after a bad-weather rideshare allowance, breakfast is included, the room basics are stronger, and luggage storage after checkout should solve Friday. I would only choose the event hotel if you want the simplest possible morning path or expect to host people in the lobby/bar.
Please hold Hampton with the work card. One king is fine. Add quiet room, itemized folio, late checkout if available, and luggage storage Friday if late checkout is not possible.

Held: Hampton Inn & Suites Minneapolis/Downtown, May 19-21, refundable one-king non-smoking room, estimated $406.18 with taxes, work card used to hold. Cancellation deadline: May 17 at 11:59 p.m. Hotel notes added: quiet room away from elevator/ice, itemized folio, late checkout if available, and Friday luggage storage if late checkout cannot be confirmed.
And for flights, does the later Friday finish change the plan?

Yes. With breakouts possibly running until 1:00, avoid the 3:20 return unless Friday becomes firmly shorter. The better target is the Delta nonstop MSP-ORD around 4:10-5:45, or any comparable nonstop after about 4:00. No flight ticketed yet; I saved that timing note with the hotel hold.
